text_sanskrit: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् । विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥ १३-२८ ॥
itrans: samaM sarveShu bhUteShu tiShThantaM parameshvaram . vinashyatsvavinashyanta.n yaH pashyati sa pashyati .. 13-28 ..
translation:
He sees (the truth) who sees the Supreme Ruler standing in all beings to be the same and sees Him within the perishing to be non-perishing (28.)
V. In all beings: that are different from each other as lower and higher, inferior and superior. The Supreme Ruler: one who is of incomprehensible powers. To be the same: to be subject to no difference whatever; to be everywhere the same Supreme Being, perfect in all excellent qualities. Within the perishing: within the beings subject to the evils of pleasure and pain, birth and death, &c. Non-Perishing: not subject to such evils. He who perceives Brahman to be such though present in all beings, is the one that has true perception or wisdom. (28). 
A. The importance of seeing Brahman equal in everything is pointed out thus:
